text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hypocrisy of communist Akel over elections.
- Nurses threaten strike action again in state hospitals.
- British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind is visiting Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash with the consent of the government, says spokesman.
- Turks open fire in flag incident after a Greek Cypriot climed pole to remove the Turkish flag.
- Striking teachers dig in for right to teach private lessons.
- Government rejects calls to cancel Rifkind visit.
- Showdown is threatened between civil servants union Pasidy and the government over nurses demands.
- Two hundred power station workers threaten strike, seeking fringe benefits for persons engaged in dangerous work.
- Turkey is cultivating the ground for a preemptive strike against Cyprus.
- Turkish troops open fire indiscriminately in the Ayios Dhometios area.
- The Central Bank is to start examining Italcementi's application to buy 13 percent stake in Vassiliko today.
- Democratic Party leader Spyros Kyprianou accuses the foreign minister of keeping him in the dark about the government's consent to Rifkind's visit to Denktash.
